title: Rotate Image
description:
# Rotate Image

You are given an `n x n` integer matrix representing a square image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise.

You must rotate the matrix in-place. That means the same `matrix` object must be modified directly; do not allocate another `n x n` matrix and copy the answer into it.

After the rotation, the value originally at row `r` and column `c` should move to row `c` and column `n - 1 - r`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** matrix = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
**Output:** [[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]]
**Explanation:** The first column becomes the first row in reverse order.

## Example 2:

**Input:** matrix = [[5,1,9,11],[2,4,8,10],[13,3,6,7],[15,14,12,16]]
**Output:** [[15,13,2,5],[14,3,4,1],[12,6,8,9],[16,7,10,11]]
**Explanation:** Both the outer ring and the inner 2 x 2 block rotate clockwise.

## Constraints:

*   `n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length`
*   `1 <= n <= 20`
*   `-1000 <= matrix[i][j] <= 1000`

solutions.name: Transpose Then Reverse Each Row
solutions.description:
## Approach

First transpose the matrix across the main diagonal, swapping `matrix[i][j]` with `matrix[j][i]` for the upper triangle. Then reverse every row in-place.

## Key Insight

A clockwise rotation can be decomposed into two reflections: main-diagonal transposition changes rows into columns, and row reversal puts every column into the required right-to-left order.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because each cell is touched a constant number of times.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because only a few temporary variables are used.

solutions.name: Layer By Layer Four-Way Swap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Process one square ring at a time. For each offset in the ring, save the top cell, move left to top, bottom to left, right to bottom, and the saved top value to right.

## Key Insight

Every cell in a clockwise rotation belongs to a four-cell cycle. Rotating a ring is just applying those four-way cycles along the ring boundary.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because every matrix cell moves once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because each cycle only needs one saved value.

solutions.name: Reverse Rows Then Transpose
solutions.description:
## Approach

Reverse the order of the rows, which mirrors the image vertically. Then transpose across the main diagonal.

## Key Insight

A vertical reflection followed by a main-diagonal reflection is also a 90-degree clockwise rotation. This gives a second reflection-based decomposition that is still fully in-place.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because row reversal is O(n) and transposition is O(n^2).
- Space Complexity: O(1), because row references and cell swaps use only temporary variables.

solutions.name: Anti-Diagonal Transpose Then Reverse Columns
solutions.description:
## Approach

Transpose the matrix across the anti-diagonal by swapping `matrix[i][j]` with `matrix[n - 1 - j][n - 1 - i]` for cells above that diagonal. Then reverse each column vertically.

## Key Insight

The anti-diagonal reflection sends each cell to the opposite diagonal position. Reversing columns after that reflection converts the mapping into the clockwise rotation target `matrix[c][n - 1 - r]`.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because both passes are bounded by the number of cells.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the algorithm uses only scalar temporaries.

solutions.name: Quadrant Coordinate Cycles
solutions.description:
## Approach

Iterate only over the cells in the top-left half of the rotation cycles. For each selected coordinate, directly rotate its four mapped positions using the coordinate rule `(r, c) -> (c, n - 1 - r)`.

## Key Insight

The matrix can be partitioned into disjoint four-position cycles, with the center cell of odd-sized matrices left untouched. Visiting one representative from each cycle rotates the whole matrix without a layer abstraction.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n^2), because the selected representatives cover all cells through four-way cycles.
- Space Complexity: O(1), because each cycle uses one temporary value.

tests.description: Canonical 3 by 3 matrix rotates clockwise in place.
Four by four matrix checks all layers and inner cells.
Single-cell matrix is unchanged by rotation.
Two by two matrix exercises the smallest real swap.
Negative values rotate by position exactly like positive values.
All equal values make sure the method does not depend on value uniqueness.
Five by five matrix checks multiple rings and the center cell.
Boundary values rotate by position without arithmetic assumptions.
Mixed signs and zero check that every coordinate mapping is exact.
Even-sized matrix with all negative values checks inner-ring handling.
Six by six matrix checks several even rings.
